Every result of the [theory note](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/doc/theory/exact-front.md)
is a **claim** in the registry `claims.toml`, and every change to its status is a
[Conventional Knowledge Commit](https://conventional-knowledge-commits.org/): a commit whose type
(`proof`, `formalize`, `conjecture`, `refute`, `lit`, …) and footers (`Status:`, `Depends-On:`,
`Closes:`, `Disproves:`) record what it asserts and what it rests on
([`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)). The graph
below is rebuilt from those commits when the site is built.

{{< include _graph-stats.md >}}

A node's colour is its **effective status**: the weakest of its own status and of everything it
depends on, so an open or refuted claim colours every result that rests on it. Click a node to trace
its dependencies; press **Play**, or drag the slider, to replay the knowledge commits in order.

The statuses are those of the ledger:

- **machine-checked**: a clean Lean kernel proof (axioms among `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
  `Quot.sound`), recorded by a `formalize` commit that closes the claim with its declaration;
- **proved informally**: a complete written proof in the note;
- **conjectured**: open, or only sketched, in the note;
- **disproved**: refuted by a counterexample, like the claim of arXiv:2304.14659 that virtual
  cities for the shuttle situations complete the non-symmetric front (Example 5.10), or a converse
  under (S) alone (Example 4.7).

The blueprint's badges follow the same statuses: its build fails if the status cached in
`claims.toml` differs from the one this history gives.

## How it is built

`site/gen_graph.py` reads the history with [claimgraph](https://github.com/hotherio/claimgraph)
and keeps only the knowledge commits, those whose type belongs to a CKC profile. The other commits
(features, fixes, documentation) would add a node per scope and a replay step each, with no claim
status to show, so the graph and its replay are compacted to the knowledge commits. The registry
`claims.toml` gives each claim its statement and Lean declarations.
`claimgraph status . --claims claims.toml` prints the same statuses from the command line.
